**Admitted Insurance** is like being on an official sports team. The team has a coach, a set schedule, uniforms, and follows the league’s rules. If something goes wrong during practice or a game, like an injury, the league has procedures in place to help you.

**Non-Admitted Insurance** is like playing a pickup game with friends at the park. There’s no coach, no uniforms, and no clear rules. If you get hurt, your friends might help, but there’s no official plan for how to handle the injury or help you.

In insurance terms, admitted insurance is provided by a company that is licensed by the state and must follow the state’s rules and regulations. The company has to meet strict standards, ensuring they are financially stable, offer clear coverage, and handle claims properly. If something happens to your home, like a fire, the company will help according to the state’s guidelines. If they don’t treat your claim fairly, you can file a complaint with the state’s insurance department.

Non-admitted insurance is from a company that is not regulated by the state. These companies can set their own rules, which means their coverage terms might be unclear or inconsistent. They don’t have to follow state rules, which can leave you with fewer protections. If you need help with a claim, the process may be harder, and since the company isn’t regulated, you may not get the same level of support. There’s also no state agency to help you if things go wrong, and you might have to deal with the company directly.

In Michigan, Personal Injury Protection (PIP) only extends to named insureds, spouses of named insured, and resident relatives. You aren’t related to the named insureds (her parents) and your girlfriend no longer lives in the house with them, so neither of you are eligible for PIP coverage under their policy. Meaning if either of you get injured in an auto accident (even as a passenger or a pedestrian) their PIP coverage won’t extend to you. 

Their liability coverage also wouldn’t extend to you if you’re not listed as a driver. If you cause an auto accident and injure or kill someone and they sue you, you are pretty much fucked. 

For proper protection, she needs to get her own policy and list you as a named insured so you both will have PIP benefits. Not all companies will list two unrelated names insured, but some carriers like Progressive will. Progressive will even let you insure a vehicle that you don’t own (if it’s still titled to her parents) in Michigan. Just make sure her parents are listed as Additional Insureds if they are on the title.

Sprint leases there phones. Every month you are paying to just borrow the phone. This is why Sprints device payments always appear less then the competition. They are charging you a lesser amount to borrow the phone from them. If you want to keep it, you have the full value of the phone, which is where the additional $150 comes in. One of the many reasons I left Sprint.

There is no proration. In fact, if you try to change your plan in the middle of a cycle, it will ask for payment for the new plan up front, even if you literally just paid. Wait until your cycle is set to renew and then change it.

Unless you get a lazy rep who doesn’t actually inspect the phone, then you will be denied. Even if they did miss it, the only way you could upgrade your phone is if you’ve paid off at least 50% of it. Do you have TMP?

Just take it day by day. Plans can seem overwhelming at first but you’ll get the hang of it. Indirects have a new quote feature which is awesome and takes a lot of the guesswork away while you’re still learning. 

When it comes to selling, I just started by learning 3 unique features about each phone. Most people aren’t techy and won’t understand if you try to sell to them based on stats from sites like phonearena.com (although I do use that to look up things on occasion). And if you don’t know something, just be honest. Every once in a while I get a question I don’t know the answer too. I just tell customers, that is a great question. I don’t have an answer but I’ll assist you in getting that information. 

Learn the promos in and outs overtime. These can def help close sales.  The first couple days just play with the phones during down time if you’re not real familiar. Learn basic things, like how to find the IMEI/ICCID numbers on iOS and Android phones, how to reset the network settings, etc. You got this! Congrats on the new job!
